questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_Pretest_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

A side changes from 4 cm to 12 cm in a similar figure. What is the scale factor?

feedback.text: This subtracts side lengths. Scale factor is multiplicative.
Correct. The scale factor is 12 divided by 4.
This adds side lengths. Use a ratio.
This multiplies side lengths, which does not give the scale factor.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_Pretest_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.2

What is the distance from (2, 5) to (9, 5)?

feedback.text: This adds x-values. Horizontal distance is the difference.
This compares y-values instead of x-values.
This uses one coordinate instead of the distance.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_Pretest_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.4

A rectangle is 8 ft by 6 ft. What is its area?

feedback.text: This adds dimensions. Area requires multiplication.
The number is correct, but area uses square units.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_Pretest_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.5

Which situation asks for surface area?

feedback.text: Correct. Wrapping covers outside faces, so it asks for surface area.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_Pretest_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.6

A prism is 3 ft by 4 ft by 5 ft. What is its volume?

feedback.text: Correct. Volume = 3 x 4 x 5 = 60 cubic ft.
The number is correct, but volume uses cubic units.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_Pretest_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.7

A right triangle has legs 5 and 12. What is the hypotenuse?

feedback.text: This adds the legs. Use the Pythagorean Theorem.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_Pretest_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.4; MLA.MCR.GM.6

Which unit should label volume?

Question ID: MCR_U06_Pretest_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.1; MLA.MCR.GM.3

On a scale drawing, 1 inch represents 6 feet. What does 4 inches represent?

Question ID: MCR_U06_Pretest_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.4 through MLA.MCR.GM.6

A design volume must be at most 80 cubic ft. The calculated volume is 75 cubic ft. What is true?

feedback.text: The units match, so it can be checked.
Correct. 75 is less than or equal to 80.
The problem is about volume, so cubic feet are appropriate.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U06_Pretest_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.GM.7

Which ratio compares opposite to hypotenuse?

feedback.text: Correct. Sine compares opposite to hypotenuse.
Perimeter is not a trigonometric ratio.
